target.artifact: repository-host proposal fingerprint pin race canary

problem: The discovery dedup library is proven only with a local fs.open('wx') race; the canonical GitHub repository path coordination/opportunities/proposal-claims/** has not demonstrated host create-if-absent exclusivity, loser collision evidence, and no-overwrite behavior under an actual race.
acceptance: Two or more concurrent attempts for one fingerprint yield exactly one durable repository pin.
Losers receive collision evidence and do not overwrite the winner.
Source proposals and lineage remain preserved.
No queue or authority promotion occurs.
title: Canary repository-host proposal pin races
mission: Exercise the canonical GitHub proposal-claim path with two or more create-if-absent attempts for the same deterministic fingerprint, persist winner/loser host receipts, and prove that collision handling preserves the winning bytes and never promotes queue or product authority.

regression_prevention.reason: The existing implementation proves local filesystem exclusivity but explicitly leaves repository-host atomicity unverified; a host canary falsifies the assumption before stress-verification or production graduation relies on it.

information_gain.reason: The canary distinguishes library correctness from the actual GitHub Contents API collision semantics used by identical /wc workers.

unblock_value.reason: Repository-host evidence closes the explicit remaining boundary of O-SWARM-DISCOVERY-DEDUP-BUILD-V1 and strengthens the evidence base for broad worker stress verification.

falsification: Two create-if-absent attempts both report success for one canonical fingerprint.
A losing attempt overwrites or mutates the winning pin bytes.
Loser collision evidence cannot identify the existing winning path/fingerprint.
The canary mutates queue authority, Current, Human Accepted or Served state.
dedup_note: Prepared universal-swarm work is currently saturated or dependency-blocked. The inspected discovery implementation's RETURN explicitly names this repository-host canary as its remaining boundary; no matching canonical fingerprint existed immediately before pin creation.
